dedupe_keys.name: active and disused telecommunication cables in the belgian part of the north sea rbins belgian marine data centre

description: The Belgian Marine Data Centre at the Royal Belgian Institute of Natural Sciences keeps two metadata records, with DOIs, for submarine telecommunication cables in the Belgian part of the North Sea. The first gives the as-built location of active telecommunication cables, verified in 2010. The second gives the location of disused telecommunication cables still on the seabed. The records, in the institute's GeoNetwork catalogue and harvested to the Belgian and European portals, were last updated in June and September 2026, with temporal extents from 2014. They form part of the marine spatial information used for the Belgian marine spatial plan, alongside power cables, pipelines and wind farm areas. Coverage: the Belgian part of the North Sea, including the routes of international cables landing at the Belgian coast. Format and access: metadata are open, and the records state that no conditions apply to use under CC BY 4.0, but the cable geometry itself is withheld for security reasons and available on request. Caveats: the geometry is not openly downloadable; active cables were verified in 2010 and newer cables may be missing; cable names, owners and capacities are not described in the metadata. Simulation uses: exposure of subsea cables to anchoring, fishing, dredging and offshore construction in a crowded shelf sea, and landing-point dependencies for Belgian international connectivity. Related records: the TeleGeography submarine cable map gives global cable routes; the Rijkswaterstaat North Sea cables layer covers the Dutch sector with similar restrictions.
licence: CC BY 4.0 (stated in metadata); geometry withheld, on request
name: Active and disused telecommunication cables in the Belgian part of the North Sea (RBINS Belgian Marine Data Centre)
notes: Metadata read on 2026-09-26 through data.europa.eu and the RBINS GeoNetwork XML record (abstract, constraints, the 'data withheld for security reasons - available on request' distribution). The link to the marine spatial plan is inferred, not stated in the record.
